title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Hydrogen (H, Z=1) is the interval [1.00784,1.00811]
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Hydrogen (H, Z=1) as [1.00784,1.00811], with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 1, symbol H, as Hydrogen. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Hydrogen as the interval [1.00784,1.00811]. This interval is the set of atomic-weight values NIST assigns to normal materials. It is not the uncertainty of one weighing. Modified isotopic compositions may be found in commercially available material because the material has been subjected to an undisclosed or inadvertent isotopic fractionation. Substantial deviations in atomic weight of the element from that given in the table can occur. Isotope rows in the same file: H-1 relative atomic mass 1.00782503223(9), isotopic composition 0.999885(70); D-2 relative atomic mass 2.01410177812(12), isotopic composition 0.000115(70); T-3 relative atomic mass 3.0160492779(24), isotopic composition blank. A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
